column1: # A multi-node devnet convergence soak: the contention regime's status samples.
# The companion to devnet-convergence-samples.tsv, and the harder question. The
# same four zycordd processes on the dev engine behind the same chaos proxy, but
# EVERY miner mines for the whole run rather than all but one being stopped
# before anything is checked. That is the state a live network is actually in,
# and under it tip agreement is neither expected nor required: two branches of
# equal work are entitled to disagree, and do.
# What is required is that every node's history BELOW the reorg horizon is a
# prefix of one chain, checked cumulatively throughout rather than once at the
# end, so a divergence that is created and then reorged away is still caught.
# The run: 199 kills, 368 partitions over 50 minutes. It ended
#   history: 744 heights verified to 744 (network reached 1000);
#     3.96 nodes per height on average, 33 heights compared across fewer than 4
#   deepest observed reorg: 3 blocks (horizon 256)
#   billing law: 874 certificate inclusions across 1000 blocks, no duplicates
#   load: 2357 certificates submitted, 2357 accepted
#   liveness: no node died unbidden (11960 state samples)
# 744 heights verified with no divergence is the result. The 33 partial
# comparisons are heights where a node was mid-kill and could not answer; they
# are reported rather than hidden, because a run that mostly talked to three
# nodes must not read like one that talked to four.
# Latency: trail p50=0, p90=0, p99=1, max=3 blocks across 795 node-samples --
# TIGHTER than the single-miner regime's p99=2/max=11, which is not a claim that
# contention is easier. The machine was under load average 6-19 here against
# 8-47 there, and that difference alone plausibly accounts for it. Do not read
# these two regimes against each other; read each against its own conditions.
# On memory, read the FLOOR and not the peak. Node a shows a peak of 183 MB at
# t=1830 and was at 45 MB by the next sample fifteen seconds later; it did the
# same at t=2565, 122 MB down to 40 MB. Both are single-sample transients that
# fully reclaim -- a collection caught mid-cycle. The floor per ten-minute window
# was 15.2, 17.1, 12.6, 22.0, 24.2 MB while the chain grew from height 276 to
# 1000, and it FELL in the middle of that. Threads stayed at 12-13 and
# descriptors at 20 throughout. Nothing here grows without bound.
# Columns: seconds since sampling began, node, whether its RPC answered, height,
# blocks behind the highest node, resident memory KB, threads, open descriptors,
# data directory KB, first eight bytes of tip. reachable=false with height 0 is
# a node the harness had killed and not yet restarted.
